events.title: Phoenix LiveView announced
events.summary: José Valim announced Phoenix LiveView on September 4, 2018 at ElixirConf US — real-time server-rendered UI over WebSockets without writing JavaScript.
events.about: LiveView let Elixir developers build interactive dashboards, forms, and chats with server-side state — sending HTML diffs over the wire. It influenced Rails Hotwire and HTMX by showing that SPAs were not the only path to rich UIs.

narrative.whyChosen: LiveView pioneered server-driven reactive UIs in a mainstream web framework.
narrative.whyImportant: It reduced frontend complexity for teams that wanted interactivity without React.
narrative.problemSolved: Real-time UIs seemed to require JavaScript SPAs and duplicated state on client and server.

events.title: Cypress leaves beta
events.summary: Cypress officially left beta on September 20, 2018 — marking 1.0 stability after years of development and millions of npm downloads.
events.about: The GA release signaled Cypress was production-ready for front-end E2E testing — time-travel debugging, automatic waiting, and real browser execution. Teams migrated from flaky Selenium suites to `cy.visit` and `cy.get` for React and Vue apps.

narrative.whyChosen: Cypress GA validated in-browser E2E testing as an enterprise-ready practice.
narrative.whyImportant: It set the reliability bar that Playwright later extended to multi-browser testing.
narrative.problemSolved: Teams hesitated to adopt Cypress in CI while the framework was still labeled beta.

events.title: iPhone XS released
events.summary: Apple began selling the iPhone XS on September 21, 2018 — refining the iPhone X with the A12 Bionic and improved cameras.
events.about: The XS established the annual 'pro' tier cadence with better neural engine performance for Core ML and computational photography APIs developers could leverage in camera and AR apps.

narrative.whyChosen: The XS iterated the premium iPhone template with a much faster neural engine.
narrative.whyImportant: On-device ML performance became a realistic baseline for iOS camera and AR apps.
narrative.problemSolved: Premium iPhones needed better ML silicon for real-time vision workloads.

events.title: Java 11 LTS released
events.summary: Oracle and the OpenJDK community shipped Java 11 on September 25, 2018 — the first long-term support release in the new six-month cadence, with a built-in HTTP client and removed Java EE modules.
events.about: Java 11 became the migration target after Java 8 for teams that needed LTS without Oracle's paid support trap. It extended `var` to lambda parameters (introduced in Java 10), added a built-in HTTP client, and single-file `java` launch scripts modernized everyday Java development.

narrative.whyChosen: Java 11 was the bridge LTS between the Java 8 era and modern 17/21 releases.
narrative.whyImportant: It established the six-month feature release + LTS every three years model.
narrative.problemSolved: After Java 9/10's rapid releases, enterprises needed a stable LTS with modern features.
